criterion_notes.c1: The Table of Contents and Introduction confirm that the book examines household and community drinking-water availability, sufficiency, accessibility, and safety in the southern West Bank.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: passes prima facie based on the Table of Contents and Introduction, as the book examines international human rights and humanitarian law, the Oslo Accords, Palestinian Water Law No 3/2002, Israeli Water Law 1959, Israeli case law, and Israeli Military Orders in relation to water access in the West Bank. Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: unclear because Chapters 1–7 (pp. 8–196) are omitted from the retrieved publisher preview PDF; without Chapters 5 and 6, we cannot determine whether the empirical case study examines a concrete rule-type mechanism directly governing service access (such as military orders, permitting/connection rules, or regulatory allocation) versus general macro-conflict or doctrinal human-rights commentary.
criterion_notes.c3: The Introduction (p. 7) states that Chapter 6 reports a qualitative empirical case study based on 45 semi-structured interviews in the southern West Bank, indicating the full book is not purely doctrinal commentary; however, Chapter 6 (pp. 137–172, including 'Empirical study – design and methods') is completely missing from the retrieved PDF excerpt, preventing direct methodological assessment.

evidence_quotes.quote: The book provides a legal analysis of the right to water, combined with a qualitative case study which investigates and evaluates enjoyment of the right by people ‘on the ground’.

Chapter 5 continues the legal analysis but at a national and bilateral level and considers the provisions for a right to water under the bilateral agreements between Israel and the OPTs, commonly known as the Oslo Accords, and under applicable domestic law of Palestine and Israel.

The material presented is gathered from 45 semi-structured interviews which took place in the southern West Bank and which are based around questions related to the key elements of the right to water: availability, accessibility and safety;
The right to water in the Occupied Palestinian Territories (West Bank) Part III – A case study in the Southern West Bank 137
